items.title: Quiet Dishes
items.topic: using non-requests as conflict avoidance in shared life
items.angle: If you won’t ask directly, you don’t just avoid a fight-you train the room to keep running on your silence.

items.title: Let-Me-Know Follow-Ups
items.angle: If your message avoids the decision, people can’t respond without risking being wrong-so add a deadline and two usable options.

items.title: The Missing Detail
items.topic: Embarrassment dissolves when you name the exact missing thing
items.angle: The threshold doesn’t open for vague apologies-it opens when you offer one usable detail, no bargaining for forgiveness.

items.title: Polite Vagueness Is a Cost
items.topic: Sending the plain request instead of smoothing it into ambiguity
items.angle: You’re allowed to send the sentence you actually mean; the “just checking” edit mostly buys you more waiting.

items.title: Emoji Silence, Live Schedule
items.topic: Emoji reactions replacing real replies in group chats
items.angle: A reaction is a social dodge: it acknowledges presence without taking the small, embarrassing step of committing to the answer.

items.title: Sometime Next Week
items.topic: vague scheduling becoming someone else’s commitment
items.angle: When you dodge a date, you quietly give it away-then you’re stuck negotiating the consequences.

items.title: Affectionate Exit
items.topic: Post-fight texts used to dodge repair
items.angle: An affectionate sign-off after a fight often functions as an off-ramp from accountability, not an arrival to resolution.

items.title: Sure Is a Placeholder
items.topic: When a quick yes is social relief, not commitment
items.angle: The default is “I changed my mind.” The useful frame is “I bargained for comfort, and it got scheduled.”

items.title: Rationing Attention
items.angle: When your phone pre-books your attention, generosity becomes an exception you keep having to justify.

items.title: Kind Questions, Stuck Room
items.topic: Questions that sound considerate but block the decision
items.angle: When a question can’t be answered without risk, it quietly removes responsibility from the asker-and keeps everyone waiting.

items.title: Brain-Picking Container
items.topic: Setting a time box for vague requests
items.angle: If someone asks to “pick your brain” without a decision or deadline, they’re asking for your attention-so you offer a small, specific container instead.

items.title: The Sentence Before the Sticker
items.topic: Specificity in a time-sensitive handoff beats polite vagueness
items.angle: In public, when the question has a consequence, the kindest move is the exact sentence and the paperwork that matches it.

items.title: Feedback as Permission
items.angle: If you call it feedback but you’re really waiting for permission, the delay becomes the point.

items.title: No Rush, Still Due
items.topic: The 'no rush' phrase that quietly schedules you without negotiating time
items.angle: When someone says 'no rush' right next to a deadline, they remove your ability to ask-so you end up doing the prioritizing work for them.
